facts.text: Reconstructing history is similar to assembling a jigsaw puzzle; coins, inscriptions, paintings and pottery are the pieces.
facts.quote: Reconstructing history is similar to assembling a jigsaw puzzle. Objects from the past such as coins, inscriptions, paintings and pottery act as the small, individual pieces of that puzzle.

facts.text: Sources of history are broadly classified into primary sources, secondary sources and oral sources.
facts.quote: These sources are broadly classified into primary sources, secondary sources and oral sources.

facts.text: Primary sources belong directly to the specific historical time period, e.g. inscriptions, copper plates, coins, original documents (birch-bark manuscripts, deeds, letters), weapons, temples.
facts.quote: These sources belong directly to the specific historical time period. Examples: Inscriptions, copper plates, coins, original documents (birch-bark manuscripts, deeds, letters, etc.), antique objects, weapons, ancient structures, temples, etc.

facts.text: Primary sources provide authentic information regarding the specific era.
facts.quote: When writing history, these sources provide authentic information regarding the specific era.

facts.text: Secondary sources offer information derived from the study and analysis of primary sources, e.g. history books and articles, documentaries, research papers, lectures by experts, encyclopedias.
facts.quote: These sources offer information derived from the study and analysis of primary sources. Examples : History related articles and books, documentaries, research papers, lectures by experts, encyclopedias, etc.

facts.text: Secondary sources provide a coherent and cohesive account of history and are created by researchers through careful analysis and interpretation.
facts.quote: These sources provide a coherent and cohesive account of history. These are created by researchers through careful analysis and interpretation.

facts.text: Oral sources preserve the past in oral form across generations, e.g. folktales, folk songs, tales of valor, memories of villagers and elders.
facts.quote: These sources preserve events, traditions, culture, or experiences from the past in an oral form, handed down and preserved across generations. Examples: Folktales, folk songs, Traditional compositions, Tales of valor and heroism, memories and experiences recounted by villagers and elders

facts.text: Oral sources are invaluable for understanding periods for which no written evidence exists.
facts.quote: Oral sources are invaluable for understanding the daily life, traditions and culture of periods for which no written evidence exists.

facts.text: Material sources are those that we can perceive with our eyes; in historical research they are regarded as primary sources.
facts.quote: Material sources are those that we can perceive with our eyes. ... In historical research, these objects are regarded as Primary Sources.

facts.text: Material sources include inscriptions, copper plates, old coins, weapons, pottery, sculptures, ancient buildings, forts, temples and water bodies.
facts.quote: These include inscriptions, copper plates, old coins, weapons, pottery, stone or metal sculptures, ancient buildings, forts, temples, water bodies and so forth.

facts.text: The clay, surface finish and motifs of potsherds found in excavations help to determine the specific period.
facts.quote: Potsherds discovered during excavations, the clay used to make them, their surface finish and colourful or artistic motifs help to determine the specific period.

facts.text: Excavated food grains, fruit seeds and animal bones help reconstruct the dietary habits of a period.
facts.quote: the study of excavated remains such as food grains, fruit seeds, and animal bones enables us to reconstruct the dietary habits of that specific period.

facts.text: Inscriptions give insights into the administration and the religious and social life of ancient times.
facts.quote: Inscribed inscriptions provide valuable insights into the administration, as well as the religious and social life of ancient times.

facts.text: Weapons, fortifications, palaces and ancient structures reveal defence systems, war strategies and architectural styles.
facts.quote: The study of weapons, fortifications, palaces and ancient structures reveals information regarding the defense systems, war strategies and architectural styles of the respective period.

facts.text: Old coins or seals shed light on the economy, names of rulers, religious traditions and artistic trends.
facts.quote: old coins or seals shed light on the economy, the names of rulers, religious traditions and the artistic trends.

facts.text: Sources that are available in a written form are called written sources.
facts.quote: Sources that are available in a written form are referred to as 'Written Sources'.

facts.text: During the Stone Age, the prehistoric period, humans had not learnt writing, so our knowledge of that era comes mainly from material sources.
facts.quote: During the Stone Age that is, the prehistoric period humans had not yet learnt the art of writing. Consequently, our knowledge of that era is derived primarily from material sources.

facts.text: People began expressing experiences through pictures and symbols; this marked the beginning of the art of writing.
facts.quote: people began to express their experiences and information through pictures and symbols. This marked the beginning of the art of writing.

facts.text: The period with written evidence is the Historical Period; the times before scripts developed are the Prehistoric Period.
facts.quote: The period for which written evidence is available to write history is known as the 'Historical Period.' The times during which scripts had not yet developed is referred to as the 'Prehistoric Period.'

facts.text: Written sources from ancient times are preserved at various museums, libraries and temples.
facts.quote: Written sources from ancient times are preserved at various museums, libraries and temples.

facts.text: Oral sources are passed on by word of mouth and include folktales, myths, Ovi, Povada, proverbs and folk songs.
facts.quote: Oral sources refer to information that is transmitted by word of mouth rather than writing it down. ... These sources include folktales, myths, traditional compositions like Ovi, Povada, proverbs and folk songs etc.

facts.text: Historians verify oral sources by comparative analysis and with the help of other sources.
facts.quote: when utilizing oral sources for historical research, historians verify the information, by conducting comparative analysis and with the help of other sources reconstruct history.

facts.text: The ancient period covers the time from the Stone Age to approximately the 8th century CE.
facts.quote: The ancient period covers the time period from the Stone Age to approximately 8th century CE.

facts.text: The history of the Stone Age relies entirely on material evidence from archaeological excavations.
facts.quote: The history of the Stone Age relies entirely on material evidence obtained through archaeological excavations.

facts.text: The Vedas are the most ancient sources of Indian history; at first they were not written but memorised and passed on orally.
facts.quote: The most ancient sources of Indian history are the Vedas. Initially, the Vedas were not in written form. Ancient Indians had developed a technique for memorizing and orally transmitting them.

facts.text: The four Vedas are Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda and Atharvaveda; they contain hymns in praise of the deities and sacrificial rituals.
facts.quote: The four Vedas-Rigveda, Yajurveda, Samaveda, and Atharvaveda contain hymns (songs) in praise of the deities and sacrificial rituals.

facts.text: The Brahmana texts, Aranyakas and Upanishads were composed later and help us understand ancient Indian philosophy.
facts.quote: The Brahmana texts, Aranyakas and Upanishads were composed later. These texts help us to understand ancient Indian philosophy.

facts.text: The great Indian epics Ramayana and Mahabharata are valuable sources of ancient Indian history.
facts.quote: Furthermore, Ramyana and Mahabharata, the great Indian epics are valuable sources of ancient Indian history.

facts.text: Sangham literature is the most ancient literature in the Tamil language.
facts.quote: Sangham literature is the most ancient literature in the Tamil language.

facts.text: The Buddhist texts are collectively known as Tipitaka; they contain Gautama Buddha's teachings, rules for monks and philosophical discussions, written in Pali, a Prakrit language.
facts.quote: The Buddhist texts are collectively known as 'Tipitaka'. Tipitaka contains the teachings of Gautama Buddha, rules for monks and philosophical discussions. These texts are written in Pali, a Prakrit language.

facts.text: The Jaina texts known as Agamas discuss the teachings of Vardhamana Mahavira and Ahimsa; they are written in Ardhamagadhi, a Prakrit language.
facts.quote: The teachings of Vardhamana Mahavira and the importance of Ahimsa (non-violence) are discussed in Jaina texts known as 'Agamas'. These texts are written in Ardhamagadhi, a Prakrit language.

facts.text: Emperor Ashoka conveyed his thoughts through rock and pillar inscriptions, mainly in the Brahmi script, some in Kharoshti and Aramaic.
facts.quote: Emperor Ashoka conveyed his thoughts on religious teachings and social values to his subjects through rock inscriptions and pillar inscriptions. These inscriptions are primarily carved in the Brahmi script. However, some of them also appear in Kharoshti and Aramaic scripts.

facts.text: Royal decrees on land grants and tax exemptions were inscribed on copper plates, which tell us about administrative systems.
facts.quote: royal decrees regarding land grants and tax exemptions were inscribed on copper plates. These records provide valuable insights into the administrative systems.

facts.text: Travelogues of foreign travellers describe the educational systems, religious life and social customs of ancient India.
facts.quote: Travelogues of foreign travellers are also significant sources of information regarding ancient India. They provide detailed descriptions of the educational systems, religious life, social customs, and other aspects of daily life

facts.text: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya in Mumbai houses a vast collection of artefacts related to the history of India.
facts.quote: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya in Mumbai, Maharashtra is well-known. It houses a vast collection of artefacts related to the history of India.

facts.text: The museum at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in Pune offers a glimpse of archaeological artifacts.
facts.quote: The museum at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in Pune offers a glimpse of archaeological artifacts.

facts.text: The Raja Dinkar Kelkar Museum has galleries of household objects, jewellery, weaponry, musical instruments, textiles and artworks.
facts.quote: The Raja Dinkar Kelkar Museum features galleries dedicated to a diverse range of household objects jewellery, weaponry, musical instruments, textiles and artworks.

facts.text: Other museums: Central Museum in Nagpur, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Museum in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Shri Chhatrapati Shahu Museum in Kolhapur, Shri Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Museum in Satara.
facts.quote: The Central Museum in Nagpur, Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Museum in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Shri Chhatrapati Shahu Museum in Kolhapur, Shri Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Museum in Satara

facts.text: The Shanti-Krishna Museum of Money and History is at Anjaneri (near Tryambakeshwar), Nashik district.
facts.quote: Shanti-Krishna Museum of Money and History located at Anjaneri (near Tryambakeshwar), Nashik district

facts.text: The Ajanta and Verul Caves were included in UNESCO's World Heritage List in 1983.
facts.quote: The most renowned of these heritage sites are the Ajanta and Verul Caves. They were included in the UNESCO's World Heritage List in 1983.

facts.text: The Gharapuri Caves (Elephanta Caves) near Mumbai were declared World Heritage in 1987.
facts.quote: The Gharapuri Caves (Elephanta Caves) and Kanheri Caves, located near Mumbai, are also famous. The Gharapuri caves were declared as World Heritage in 1987.

facts.text: In 2018, seventy six art deco buildings were added to the World Heritage List.
facts.quote: In 2018, seventy six art deco buildings were added to this list.

facts.text: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in Mumbai, an example of Gothic architecture of the British era, was declared a World Heritage Site in 1997.
facts.quote: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in Mumbai stands as an outstanding example of Gothic architecture of the British era. It was declared a World Heritage Site in 1997.

facts.text: The Sahyadri ranges, known as the Western Ghats, are rich in biodiversity; UNESCO recognised them as a Natural Heritage Site in 2012.
facts.quote: The Sahyadri mountain ranges of Maharashtra are known as the 'Western Ghats'. They are rich in biodiversity. In 2012, UNESCO recognised it as a Natural Heritage Site.

facts.text: UNESCO has recently recognised 12 forts as World Heritage Sites under the title Maratha Military Landscapes; 11 are in Maharashtra and Jinji is in Tamil Nadu.
facts.quote: UNESCO has recently recognized 12 forts as World Heritage Sites under the collective title 'Maratha Military Landscapes'. Out of these 11 forts are located in Maharashtra, while the fort of Jinji is situated in the state of Tamil Nadu.

facts.text: Material sources give insights into the lives, culture, traditions, games, arts and sciences of the people of that era.
facts.quote: Material sources provide insights into the lives, culture, traditions, games, arts and sciences of the people of that era.
